search_strategy: The agent ran a broad reconnaissance pass: exported the entire chat.txt (~11k lines across 12 channels) and the wiki (all pages), then used targeted grep passes on domain terms ('run identity|run_identity|identity_version|run_stamp|reconcile|RunIdentity|CachedResponseMismatch|v3-', then 'components|digest|xxh64|canonical|prompt_func_hash|...', then 'system_prompt|return_completions_object|cache_enabled|twelve|...') to locate candidate line ranges. Critically, rather than trusting single grep lines, it followed up nearly every hit with `sed -n '<range>p'` dumps of 30-90 lines to read full multi-turn exchanges in context -- this is why most facts were recovered with complete context rather than fragments. It explicitly re-derived the full component list, cross-checked the Jan herrings against their March/April reversals, and stated the supersession reasoning out loud before implementing. It also checked the wiki for a 'cache identity spec' page and confirmed none existed outside chat. IMAP mail was available per the task brief but this task's remarks are chat-only (48/48 in Mattermost), consistent with the answer key's 'this task has no wiki or mail carriers' note. Weaknesses: several sed ranges were cut short by the chosen line bounds (g4.r1.l-window-reuse, g4.r1.fix25's `cut -c1-200`), losing the tail of an exchange even when the core content was captured; and 11 of 48 remarks were never surfaced at all, though every fact they carried was independently covered by a redundant remark elsewhere (the plant's designed spread meant no single miss was fatal).
